MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes exceeding two pages in length will not be considered, please visit the new resume guidance for more information. READ ALL SECTIONS OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IN ITS ENTIRETY. THIS INFORMATION IS CRUCIAL TO SUBMITTING A SUCCESSFUL APPLICATION. Applicants must qualify for the series and grade of the posted position. Experience must be IT related; the experience may be demonstrated by paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training (for example, IT certification), as appropriate. Your resume must provide sufficient experience and/or education, knowledge, skills, abilities, and proficiency of any required competencies to perform the specific position for which you are applying. To qualify for the 2210 IT Specialist series, the applicant must demonstrate the following competencies: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; know about available products and services; and is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Minimum Qualifications: Grade 13 (Bargaining Unit Position) To qualify at the GS-13 level, you must have specialized experience at the GS-12 level, or equivalent, developing and maintaining web applications using React.js and Node.js; building and integrating RESTful APIs and working with databases such as PostgreSQL or MongoDB; writing clean, maintainable code and using version control tools like Git or Bitbucket; collaborating with team members in an agile environment to deliver new features and resolve issues; writing and maintaining unit and integration tests; troubleshooting and debugging web applications; familiarity with cloud platforms (such as AWS or Azure) and CI/CD pipelines is preferred. Minimum Qualifications: Grade 14 To qualify at the GS-14 level, you must have specialized experience at the GS-13 level, or equivalent, designing, developing, and maintaining large-scale, responsive web applications using React.js, CSS, and JSON; building and integrating RESTful APIs using Node.js and Express.js to support enterprise-level web applications; collaborating with cross-functional teams to define, design, and deliver new features in a fast-paced, agile environment; writing clean, maintainable, and efficient code following Test-Driven Development (TDD) practices, including unit and integration testing with React Testing Library (RTL) and other popular testing libraries; utilizing Git or Bitbucket for version control and collaborating with team members using Visual Studio Code; integrating and managing PostgreSQL and MongoDB databases, including writing advanced SQL queries and working with data formats such as JSON and XML; developing and maintaining API documentation using Swagger UI; implementing and maintaining security best practices, including authentication and authorization for web applications; ensuring web applications are compliant with Section 508 accessibility standards; troubleshooting, debugging, and upgrading existing systems, including resolving production outages and issues by analyzing Splunk logs and Dynatrace; integrating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solutions into robust, API-driven architectures for real-time connectivity with existing systems; conducting performance analysis and tuning to optimize memory and CPU consumption. Minimum Qualifications: Grade 15 To qualify at the GS-15 level, you must have specialized experience at the GS-14 level, or equivalent, designing, developing, and maintaining large-scale, responsive web applications using React.js, CSS, and JSON; building and integrating RESTful APIs using Node.js and Express.js to support enterprise-level web applications; collaborating with cross-functional teams to define, design, and deliver new features in a fast-paced, agile environment; writing clean, maintainable, and efficient code following Test-Driven Development (TDD) practices, including unit and integration testing with React Testing Library (RTL) and other popular testing libraries; utilizing Git or Bitbucket for version control and collaborating with team members using Visual Studio Code; integrating and managing PostgreSQL and MongoDB databases, including writing advanced SQL queries and working with data formats such as JSON and XML; developing and maintaining API documentation using Swagger UI; implementing and maintaining security best practices, including authentication and authorization for web applications; ensuring web applications are compliant with Section 508 accessibility standards; troubleshooting, debugging, and upgrading existing systems, including resolving production outages and issues by analyzing Splunk logs and Dynatrace; integrating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solutions into robust, API-driven architectures for real-time connectivity with existing systems; conducting performance analysis and tuning to optimize memory and CPU consumption. PLEASE NOTE: This specialized experience is REQUIRED and must be explicitly documented/described in your resume, or you will be disqualified from further consideration. You may be asked to take a Code Signal online assessment. Qualification standards and additional information for this position can be found here: http://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/2200/information-technology-it-management-series-2210-alternative-a/

The evaluation you receive is based on your responses to the online assessment questions completed during the application process. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Serving Those Who Serve
MajorDuties: Serves as the UX Engineer for Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) enterprise digital platforms. Reports directly to the Digital Product and User Experience Manager and supports the design, development, implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of MCCS digital experiences. Applies knowledge of user experience principles, front-end development practices, accessibility requirements, content management systems, and web technologies to support enterprise digital platforms. Collaborates with product management, stakeholders, developers, contractors, and content contributors to implement approved enhancements, maintain platform functionality, and improve the overall user experience. Supports enterprise website platforms and digital services through front-end development, content management system administration, user training, platform support, testing, and quality assurance activities. Assists with evaluating user needs, troubleshooting technical issues, implementing enhancements, and maintaining digital experiences that support organizational objectives and customer needs. MAJOR DUTIES: UX Engineering and Platform Development - Designs, develops, and maintains digital experiences utilizing modern web technologies, content management systems, and established development standards. - Implements approved requirements, interface designs, wireframes, prototypes, and content structures into functional digital solutions. - Develops and maintains responsive user interfaces, navigation systems, and front-end functionality across MCCS digital platforms. - Assists with troubleshooting, maintenance, enhancement, and support of enterprise digital platforms and web applications. - Supports testing, quality assurance, and validation activities to ensure platform functionality and usability. Content Management Systems and Platform Operations - Configures, maintains, and supports enterprise content management systems and associated platform functionality. - Assists installation personnel and platform users with content management, publishing workflows, and platform administration activities. - Monitors assigned digital platforms and coordinates corrective actions or support efforts to maintain platform performance, availability, and continuity of service. - Supports content implementation, platform configuration, and ongoing operational activities across enterprise digital platforms. Training, User Adoption, and Knowledge Management - Develops and maintains training materials, user guides, standard operating procedures, knowledge base articles, and support documentation. - Coordinates and delivers training sessions, workshops, demonstrations, and onboarding activities for platform users and stakeholders. - Serves as the primary coordinator for CMS user training, onboarding activities, training materials, and operational support resources. - Assists users with platform adoption, troubleshooting, and utilization of established workflows, processes, and best practices. Accessibility, Usability, and Continuous Improvement - Implements established accessibility standards, user experience requirements, and front-end development best practices. - Supports usability evaluations and identifies opportunities to improve user experiences across digital platforms. - Reviews user feedback, support requests, and platform usage trends to identify enhancement opportunities. - Assists with analytics implementation and validation of user experience improvements. Stakeholder Support and Collaboration - Provides technical consultation and support to MCCS stakeholders, installation personnel, and platform users. - Collaborates with developers, designers, system administrators, cybersecurity personnel, contractors, and other stakeholders to support successful platform delivery and operations. - Assists with requirements gathering, solution planning, testing, implementation, and issue resolution activities. Provides World Class Customer Service with an emphasis on courtesy. Takes action to solve problems quickly. Alerts the supervisor or proper point of contact for help when problems arise. Adheres to safety regulations and standards. Promptly reports workplace hazards, injuries, occupational illnesses, and property damage resulting from workplace mishaps. Adheres to established standards supporting Equal Employment Opportunity principles and prevention of sexual harassment. Performs other duties as assigned. This is a white-collar position where occasional lifting up to 20 lbs. may be required.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the (GS-12) grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Analyze business needs and design, develop, test, implement, and support enterprise software solutions that improve organizational effectiveness; 2) Lead complex technology projects by defining requirements, guiding technical decisions, coordinating stakeholders, and resolving technical challenges; 3) Manage AWS-hosted application environments and infrastructure supporting Liferay and other enterprise web platforms to ensure secure and reliable operations. 4) Direct the development, modernization, and maintenance of public-facing and internal websites, web applications, and digital services. Your experience must reflect skill in the following areas: attention to detail, customer service, oral communication, and problem solving.1) Attention to Detail-Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. IT related experience demonstrating this competency includes: Reviewing the information technology-related work of others to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. 2) Customer Service-Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. YOUR FULL RESUME WILL NEED TO BE UPLOADED TO YOUR USAJOBS PROFILE USING THE DOCUMENT TYPE "OTHER DOCUMENTS". This position is in the Professional Work Category at the Full Performance Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure. Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Civilian Employees of the Organization Applying to Cyber Excepted Service (CES) Positions Organization is defined as current, permanent ARCYBER/NETCOM employees only. Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe one year of applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Applicable experience would be demonstrated by Organizing system analysis for routine and recurring system designs to maintain web and database applications; facilitating in dept system analysis to accomplish design and programming of web development assignments; and evaluating system documentation in compliance with agency standards. The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing work independently that rarely requires editing or review by others. (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving simple and routine problems, questions, or complaints and providing support and guidance to customers on non-routine issues; serving as a primary resource for customers, requesting assistance with complex issues when necessary; and participating in meetings and providing advice to customers in own area of expertise. (3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: expressing facts and ideas in a clear, concise, convincing, and organized manner; clearly conveying moderately complex ideas, concepts, and information to customers; exhibiting active listening by demonstrating understanding of audience comments and/or questions. (4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: identifying and solving problems by gathering and applying information from a variety of materials or sources that provide several alternatives; recognizing and taking action to address non-routine problems; soliciting feedback from multiple stakeholders to understand an issue or problem and accurately assess its root causes and potential solutions; seeking supervisory review where appropriate. OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree from an accredited or pre-accredited institution in computer science, engineering, information science, information systems management, mathematics, operations research, statistics, or technology management; or, three full years of graduate education from an accredited or pre-accredited institution that provided a minimum of 24 semester hours in one or more of the fields identified above and required the development or adaptation of applications, systems, or networks.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: READ ALL SECTIONS OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IN ITS ENTIRETY. THIS INFORMATION IS CRUCIAL TO SUBMITTING A SUCCESSFUL APPLICATION. Resumes exceeding two pages in length will not be considered, please visit the new resume guidance for more information. If you are qualifying based on education please make sure you follow the instructions in the Education Section of this announcement including uploading a transcript with an award/confer date failure to due so can disqualify you for further consideration. Applicants must qualify for the series and grade of the posted position. Experience must be IT related; the experience may be demonstrated by paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training (for example, IT certification), as appropriate. Your resume must provide sufficient experience and/or education, knowledge, skills, abilities, and proficiency of any required competencies to perform the specific position for which you are applying. As an IT Specialist (APPSW), You will play a pivotal role in Providing technical support in the preparation, creation, testing, implementation, evaluation, and ongoing support of business applications and technology solutions that meet agency objectives. To qualify for the 2210 IT Specialist series, the applicant must demonstrate the following competencies: Attention to Detail (Level 4, Advanced) - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail Customer Service (Level 4, Advanced) - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Decision Making (Level 3, Intermediate) - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management (Level 4, Advanced) - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills (Level 4, Advanced) - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations Oral Communication (Level 3, Intermediate) - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving (Level 4, Advanced) - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork (Level 4, Advanced) - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. Technical Competence (Level 4, Advanced) - Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues. Specialized Experience Applicants must have specialized experience that is directly related to the work of the position and have equipped them with the competencies required to successfully perform the duties of the role. These knowledge, skills, and abilities/competencies are normally attained through the equivalent of one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level of the position being filled. To qualify at the GS-07 level, you must have specialized experience at the GS-06 level, or equivalent. This IT-related experience must demonstrate proficiency in the following: Experience working with SQL or NoSQL databases to help support business applications. Experience assisting with web applications, such as using React.js or Node.js RESTful APis. Experience helping to troubleshoot and debug web applications in a team setting. Experience preparing or updating basic technical documents, such as user guides or process notes, and communicating information clearly to others. To qualify at the GS-09 level, you must have specialized experience at the GS-07 level, or equivalent. This IT-related experience must demonstrate proficiency in the following: Experience supporting business applications by working with SQL or NoSQL databases, including assisting with data management tasks. Experience helping to develop or maintain web applications using technologies such as React.js or Node.js RESTful APis. Experience troubleshooting and resolving issues in web applications, including identifying problems and working with others to find solutions. Experience preparing and updating technical documentation, such as user guides or process instructions, and communicating technical information to team members. To qualify at the GS-11 level, you must have specialized experience at the GS-09 level, or equivalent. This IT-related experience must demonstrate proficiency in the following: Experience modernizing IT infrastructure and supporting IT systems by implementing, maintaining, or troubleshooting enterprise-level data platforms and business applications, ensuring reliable and scalable operations. Experience designing, developing, and maintaining web applications using modem frameworks such as React.js or Node.js RESTful APis, including writing and maintaining unit and integration tests to ensure software quality. Experience applying software development lifecycle (SDLC) methodologies and utilizing both modem and legacy programming languages to deliver technical solutions that meet organizational objectives. Experience preparing and maintaining technical documentation, such as system diagrams, user guides, and deployment guides, and effectively communicating technical information both orally and in writing to multidisciplinary teams. To qualify at the GS-12 level, you must have specialized experience at the GS-11 level, or equivalent. This IT-related experience must demonstrate proficiency in the following: Experience modernizing IT infrastructure and supporting IT systems by implementing, maintaining, or troubleshooting enterprise-level data platforms and business applications, ensuring reliable and scalable operations. Experience designing, developing, and maintaining web applications using modem frameworks such as React.js or Node.js RESTful APis, including writing and maintaining unit and integration tests to ensure software quality. Experience applying software development lifecycle (SDLC) methodologies and utilizing both modem and legacy programming languages to deliver technical solutions that meet organizational objectives. Experience preparing and maintaining technical documentation, such as system diagrams, user guides, and deployment guides, and effectively communicating technical information both orally and in writing to multidisciplinary teams. Qualification standards and additional information for this position can be found here: http://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/2200/information-technology-it-management-series-2210-alternative-a/

You must submit your transcripts according to the application submission details of this announcement. Documents will not be accepted via email or regular mail. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You must have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the competencies listed below: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. Technical Competence - Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues. AND in addition to meeting the above competencies, you must also meet the specialized experience and time in grade for the General Schedule (GS) listed below in order to be found qualified for the position. Current Federal employees must have served 52 weeks at the next lower grade or equivalent grade band in the Federal service. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of this announcement. To qualify for this position at the GS-11 level, you must possess one full year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-09 level in the Federal government, which has equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. Experience may be obtained in the federal government, a state or local government, or private sector, and must demonstrate the following: Ensuring the reliability of Web-based and SharePoint applications; AND Coordinating with stakeholders to exchange information and resolve issues; AND Installing and configuring system software; AND Monitoring system performance and maintaining system documentation. To qualify for this position at the GS-12 level, you must possess one full year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-11 level in the Federal government, which has equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. Experience may be obtained in the federal government, a state or local government, or private sector, and must demonstrate the following: Managing and enhancing Web-based and SharePoint applications; AND Coordinating with stakeholders to resolve technical issues; AND Installing and configuring software to ensure system reliability and security compliance; AND Monitoring system performance and providing feedback on system documentation. Please read the following important information to ensure we have everything we need to consider your application: Do not copy and paste the duties, specialized experience, or occupational assessment questionnaire from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. Please limit your resume to two pages. The USAJOBS database will not allow an applicant to submit an application that includes a resume over two pages. Your resume serves as the basis for experience related qualification determinations, and you must highlight your most relevant and significant work experience and education (if applicable), as it relates to this job opportunity. Please use your own words, be clear, and specific when describing your work history. We cannot make assumptions regarding your experience. Are you qualifying based on your work experience? Qualifications are based on your ability to demonstrate in your resume that you possess one year of the specialized experience for this announcement at a comparable scope and responsibility. To ensure all of the essential information is in your resume, we encourage you to use the USAJOBS online Resume Builder. If you choose to use your own resume, it must contain the following information organized by experience/position: (1) job title, (2) name of employer, (3) start and end dates of each period of employment (from MM/DD/YY to MM/DD/YY), (4) detailed description of duties performed, accomplishments, and related skills, and (5) hours worked per week (part-time employment will be prorated in crediting experience). Federal experience/positions must also include the grade level, occupational series and dates in which you held each grade level. Are you a current or former FEMA Reservist/DAE employee? To accurately credit your experience from intermittent positions and Reservist Deployments, you must list the dates (from MM/DD/YY to MM/DD/YY) of deployments that are relevant to your qualifying experience, along with the job title and specific duties you were responsible for during each deployment. Determining length of General or Specialized Experience is dependent on the above information. Failure to provide the above information in your resume may result in your application being found "not qualified." Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills, and provides valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. For additional information on crediting experience and/or education, please reference the OPM General Schedule Qualification Standards Are you qualifying under Veterans Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA)? To be eligible for a VEOA appointment, the veteran must 1) be a preference eligible; or 2) be a veteran separated after 3 or more years of continuous active service performed under honorable conditions. In addition, you must submit the supporting documents listed under the required documents section of this announcement. (Note: Veteran's preference does not apply under Merit Promotion procedures. View VEOA information on Feds Hire Vets.) Due weight will be given to performance appraisals and incentive awards in merit promotion selection decisions in accordance with 5 CFR 335.103(b)(3).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is calling on those who want to help protect American interests and secure our Nation. DHS Components work collectively to prevent terrorism; secure borders and our transportation systems; protect the President and other dignitaries; enforce and administer immigration laws; safeguard cyberspace; and ensure resilience to disasters. We achieve these vital missions through a workforce spanning hundreds of occupations. Make an impact; join DHS. FEMA is calling all problem-solvers, relationship builders, and leaders! FEMA is a mission-driven, people-focused Agency. Our mission is to help people before, during, and after disasters. We coordinate with other federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial partners to make sure America is equipped to prepare for and respond to disasters. Everyday FEMA employees are inspired by that mission and are working tirelessly to make a difference. Come join us in a rewarding career where you can help make our nation safer, stronger, and more prepared! Visit www.careers.fema.gov for more information.
MajorDuties: What will I do in this position if hired? In this position, you will serve as an Information Technologist Specialist (INET) in the Reslience, National Preparedness Directorate, National Disaster & Emergency Management University. Typical assignments include: Performing Web Manager duties including total quality management encompassing technical consultation, implementation of content, quality, and style; adherence to industry and agency standards, technical development of new functionality including database management systems and communications technologies; maintenance of security; and assistance with user instruction, education, and support. Providing consultation to programmers/analysts in program development, testing, and implementation of new or modified programs related to web technologies. Reviewing and making recommendations on web related information technology infrastructure upgrades. What else do I need to know? At FEMA, our mission is to help people before, during and after disasters, and every employee at FEMA has a role in emergency management. Every FEMA employee has regular and recurring emergency management responsibilities, though not every position requires routine deployment to disaster sites. All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description. Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions. Promotion Potential: Future promotions will be dependent on your ability to perform the duties at a higher level, the continuing need for an employee assigned to the higher level, and administrative approval.

To meet those standards, all selected applicants must undergo, successfully pass, and maintain a background investigation for Public Trust/High as a condition of placement into this position. For more information on background investigations for Federal jobs please visit OPM Investigations. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. Please ensure you meet the qualification requirements described below. Key Requirements: You must be a U.S. citizen to apply for this position. You must successfully pass a background investigation. Selective Service registration required. Current federal employees must meet time-in-grade requirements. You must be able to obtain and maintain a Government credit card. You must be able to deploy with little or no advance notice to anywhere in the United States and its territories for an extended period of time. Please review the Additional Information section for additional key requirements.

MajorDuties: What will I do in this position if hired? In this position, you will serve as an Information Technologist Specialist (INET) in the Reslience, National Preparedness Directorate, National Disaster & Emergency Management University. Typical assignments include: Performing Web Manager duties including total quality management encompassing technical consultation, implementation of content, quality, and style; adherence to industry and agency standards, technical development of new functionality including database management systems and communications technologies; maintenance of security; and assistance with user instruction, education, and support. Providing consultation to programmers/analysts in program development, testing, and implementation of new or modified programs related to web technologies. Reviewing and making recommendations on web related information technology infrastructure upgrades. What else do I need to know? At FEMA, our mission is to help people before, during and after disasters, and every employee at FEMA has a role in emergency management. Every FEMA employee has regular and recurring emergency management responsibilities, though not every position requires routine deployment to disaster sites. All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description. Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions. Promotion Potential: Future promotions will be dependent on your ability to perform the duties at a higher level, the continuing need for an employee assigned to the higher level, and administrative approval.

Details.JobSummary: Deputy Unit Chief for the IHSC Communications Unit supports the Unit Chief in leading national-level communications, staff supervision, workflow management, strategic messaging, executive communications, digital content, campaigns, and crisis/issues support. Ensures accurate, timely, audience-focused products aligned with ICE and IHSC priorities. This position is only open to current USPHS officers. USPHS Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidates are not eligible for this position.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is calling on those who want to help protect American interests and secure our Nation. DHS components work collectively to prevent terrorism; secure borders and our transportation systems; protect the President and other dignitaries; enforce and administer immigration laws, safeguard cyberspace; and ensure resilience to disasters. We achieve these vital missions through a comprehensive workforce spanning hundreds of occupations. Make an impact; join DHS. The mission of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is to protect America from the cross-border crime and illegal immigration that threaten national security and public safety. ICE focuses on smart immigration enforcement, preventing terrorism, and combating the illegal movement of people and goods. ICE is the principal investigative arm of DHS and the second largest investigative agency in the federal government. Created in 2003, through a merger of the investigative and interior enforcement elements of the U.S. Customs Service and the Immigration and Naturalization Service, ICE has more than 20,000 employees in more than 400 offices in the United States and around the world. ICE is a key component of the DHS layered approach to protecting our nation from a wide range of threats. For additional information about ICE and career opportunities, please visit www.ice.gov.
MajorDuties: DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategic Communications and Campaign Leadership Assist the Unit Chief in managing integrated, multi-channel communications strategies that support ICE Health Service Corps priorities. Lead the development of clear, compelling, and audience-focused messaging that translates complex IHSC initiatives, priorities, and program information for senior leaders, stakeholders, and diverse internal and external audiences. Develop task management standards, standardize approaches, and expectations; ensure uniform implementation across the Communications Unit; and ensure high-quality communications and customer service. Provide strategic communications support to ICE Health Service Corps leadership, including messaging, timing, targeting audience, and risk considerations. Oversee enterprise-level communications campaign strategy from concept through execution and evaluation, aligning messaging, stakeholder engagement, and performance outcomes with organizational priorities. Advise the Unit Chief and staff on communications strategy, messaging and risk considerations, including support for issues and crisis communications as needed. Writing, Content Development, and Executive Communications Assist the Unit Chief in overseeing the planning, writing, editing and production of communications content for ICE Health Service Corps, including executive communications, speeches, talking points, news releases, web content, social media and feature stories. Provide supervisory review of high-visibility communications products to ensure accuracy, clarity, consistency, and alignment with ICE and IHSC priorities. Guide staff in developing content for publications, presentations, web platforms, reports, internal campaigns, and leadership communications. Ensure complex IHSC data, initiatives, policies, and program outcomes are translated into clear, accurate, and audience-appropriate communications for leadership, employees, stakeholders, and other audiences. Review communications products to maintain consistency of voice, message, tone, and branding across communications products. Identify quality issues, provide corrective feedback, and coach staff on improving writing, editing, and product development. Digital Strategy and Institutional Communications Assist the Unit Chief in shaping and overseeing IHSC digital communications strategy across internal and external platforms, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, stakeholder needs, and mission objectives. Supervise and coordinate staff responsible for web content, social media coordination, digital engagement, and related communications products. Ensure IHSC web content is accurate, current, accessible, and aligned with institutional priorities. Apply digital content best practices, including accessibility standards and audience engagement strategies. Partner with communications and social media staff to ensure cohesive storytelling across platforms. Provide support for issues management and crisis communications, including message development and coordination with leadership. Project Management, Stakeholder Coordination, and Team Support Provide guidance for complex tasks and coordination for IHSC-wide efforts to ensure all resources are used properly, there are no duplication of efforts, and all communications requirements are satisfied. Assist the Unit Chief in managing all aspects of Unit operations, including supervising staff, assigning tasks and projects, and overseeing communications intake and workflow processes to ensure appropriate prioritization, clear expectations, balanced workloads, and timely delivery. Coordinate across design, digital, events and data visualization teams to execute high-impact communications initiatives. Ensure ICU is responsive, professional, and timely to all requests for communications services. Train, develop, coach, and assist communications specialists as needed. Develop workflows and standards to improve efficiency and consistency of communications output.
Details.Education: REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Holds a qualifying degree for the officer's category and an advanced degree, such as an M.A. or M.S., from an accredited institution, plus at least five years of professional experience relevant to the officer's category. Of the total professional experience, officer must possess at least three years of leadership, management, or administration experience. If the incumbent holds a clinical license, it is the responsibility of the incumbent to fulfill the obligation(s) of their licensing or certifying body to maintain currency. This position may be required to perform clinical activities with the scope of clinical license in times of critical needs within the agency. Knowledge of strategic communications principles and ability to develop, execute, and evaluate integrated, multi-channel communications strategies and campaigns. Skill in writing, editing, and producing clear, accurate, and compelling communications products for executive, internal, external, digital, media, and event audiences. Maintain high degree of independence, initiative, and follow through on a wide range of sensitive, complex, and program issues. Skill in advising leadership on communications strategy, messaging, timing, audience targeting, risk considerations, and issues or crisis communications. Skill in managing communications projects, intake processes, workflows, timelines, priorities, approvals, and competing deadlines. Ability to professionally interact effectively and collaborate with other IHSC, ERO, ICE, and DHS offices, as well as all levels of management. Flexibility and ability to adapt to sudden changes in schedules and work-related requirements. Skill in evaluating communications effectiveness using qualitative and quantitative information and recommending improvements.

Details.OtherInformation: This U.S. Public Health Service (PHS) position is located in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Office of the Chief of Staff, IHSC Communications Unit (ICU). The incumbent reports to the ICU chief. This is a supervisory position. The incumbent serves as the Deputy Unit Chief for ICU, a component of IHSC Headquarters. The unit manages national-level communications and partners with leadership and staff across Headquarters, detention facilities, and 24 field offices to develop and coordinate high-quality communications products. ICU receives numerous agencywide requests per month for communication product development, document creation, and editing. ICU personnel actively collaborate with all internal IHSC components, operate within a high-volume and fast-paced environment, and create products viewed nationally by stakeholders internal and external to IHSC. The incumbent supports the unit chief in overseeing the entire unit, with responsibility for managing and supervising team leads and staff by assigning work, monitoring deadlines, reviewing products, mentoring staff, and resolving workload or workflow issues. The incumbent tracks communications projects to ensure staff deliver products within established deadlines. The incumbent works with IHSC leaders, offices, field locations, and communications teams to ensure messages are clear, accurate, and consistent across the organization. In coordination with the unit chief, the incumbent advises on communication content, strategies, and processes to help the unit work efficiently, stay accountable, and produce consistent high-quality communications products. IHSC has a multi-sector, multidisciplinary workforce of more than 1,650 employees, including PHS commissioned officers, federal civil servants, and contract staff. In Fiscal Year (FY) 2025, IHSC managed a health care system that provided direct care to more than 171,000 detained aliens housed at 17 IHSC-staffed facilities nationwide. IHSC provided medical, dental, mental health, and public health services, resulting in nearly 1.4 million health care encounters in FY 2025. IHSC also managed off-site medical care for detained aliens housed in about 217 additional non-IHSC-staffed facilities. SUPERVISORY CONTROLS: The Deputy Unit Chief for the IHSC Communications Unit works under the supervision of the IHSC Communications Unit Chief. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This announcement will close at 11:59 PM (ET) on 10/17/2026. Applicants must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the close date. Minimum Qualification Requirement: Under the updated Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the IT Management Series (2210), applicants must: Meet or exceed all required general competencies at the minimum proficiency level for the GS-13 grade, Meet or exceed all required technical competencies established for this announcement for the GS-13 grade, and Demonstrate you have the required specialized experience for the position. You may be considered ineligible and removed from further consideration for the position, if you fail to meet any of the criteria above. Specialized Experience: You must demonstrate the competencies required to successfully perform the duties of the position. These competencies are normally attained through one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level of the position being filled. You may qualify for the GS-13 grade level, if you possess at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the federal sector, or the equivalent in the private sector. Specialized experience is experience that has equipped the candidate with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position. For this position your specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Designing a production Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) pipeline to ingest data from disparate sources into an enterprise environment feeding both, Structured Query Language (SQL) databases and Business Intelligence (Power BI) reporting endpoints; Implementing controls to ensure data compliance and governance standards (e.g., metadata tagging, role-based access, data cataloging) across both, cloud and on-premises environments; Implementing a testing and monitoring strategy to guarantee data integrity; AND Leading or participating orally in meetings to collect data and technical requirements. Evidence of the above specialized experience must be supported by detailed documentation of duties performed in positions held. Your resume is the key means we have for evaluating your skills, knowledge, and abilities as they relate to this position. Therefore, we encourage you to be clear and specific when describing your experience. We will not make assumptions regarding your experience or based on job titles alone. If your resume does not support your questionnaire answers, we will not allow credit for your response(s). Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Experience must be validated through the assessment process, consistent with OPM's skills-based hiring policy. Competencies Being Evaluated: Attention to Detail Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Decision Making Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. Oral Communication Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. Technical Competency Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues.

Details.SubAgencyName: Office of Data, Analytics, and Technology (ODAT)
MajorDuties: As a DATA ENGINEER GS-2210-13, the incumbent will be responsible for building and maintaining the on-premises and cloud infrastructures that collect, transform, and store data at scale while ensuring data quality, security and accessibility for data scientists, data analysts, statisticians, and business intelligence (BI) reporting platforms. Typical work assignments may include the following under supervision: Designs and maintains data pipelines that feed into different IT systems including, but not limited to, on-premises SQL and Oracle databases, Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments, BI reporting platforms, and Microsoft Office 365 Builds and maintains data pipelines for ODAT involving audit, evaluation, and investigative oversight projects Implements data architecture, governance, and compliance solutions for on-premises and cloud environments Develops production-grade extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) pipelines for ingesting and transforming large, disparate data from databases, Application Programming Interface (API)s, and web-scraped feeds Orchestrates with Airflow/Luigi and accelerates processing with Spark/PySpark or similar tools Applies advanced techniques for data modeling and analytics to meet oversight needs; and provides technical leadership in the development or modernization of IT data systems

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions, GS-1035 series. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: I have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems which has equipped me with the particular knowledge, skill, and ability to successfully perform the duties of the position. Examples of specialized experience include: Knowledge of concepts, principles, and practices of a public affairs program and written and oral communication principles, techniques, and analytical methods to perform a wide range of public affairs assignments to develop intercommunication between the agency and a variety of publics. Knowledge of the organization's operations and functions sufficient to communicate accurate information and modify standard methods and adapt approaches in the development of new information materials to meet organizational needs. Knowledge of the concepts, principles, policies and practices of visual information activities, which may include illustrations, photography, presentations, television/motion picture production, and base cable access television. OR EDUCATION: I have successfully completed a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree OR 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree OR LL.M., if related in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position, such as Communications. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: I have less than the full amount of specialized experience required but I have more than 2 years of graduate level education with a major or subject area related to the position to be filled. Therefore, I have a combination of experience and education. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of concepts, principles, and practices of a public affairs program and written and oral communication principles, techniques, and analytical methods to perform a wide range of public affairs assignments to develop intercommunication between the agency and a variety of stakeholders. 2. Knowledge of the organization's operations and functions sufficient to communicate accurate information and modify standard methods and adapt approaches in the development of new information materials to meet organizational needs. 3. Knowledge of the concepts, principles, policies and practices of visual information activities, which may include illustrations, photography, presentations, television/motion picture production, and base cable access television. 4. Skill in gathering, evaluating, and interpreting data to identify potential problems, arrive at valid conclusions, and offer meaningful recommendations and/or resolutions. 5. Skill in working with people to establish and maintain effective working relationships with groups interested in or affected by public affairs programs or policies, and producing written information conveying complex information to publics with different levels of understanding. 6. Ability to plan and develop news stories, features, and quasi-technical articles. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You must meet the United States Office of Personnel Management's (OPM) qualification requirements (including specialized experience and/or educational requirements) for the advertised position. You must meet all eligibility and qualifications requirements by the closing date of the job announcement. OPM Qualifications Standards are available at Administrative and Management Positions. Specialized Experience is experience that has equipped applicants with the particular knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled. o be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade level in the federal service. For this position, the next lower grade level is a GS-12. Specialized experience for this position includes: Experience developing and executing web communications strategies to support communication goals and improve the customer experience online; Experience analyzing website traffic statistics, usability-testing data, customer feedback, and/or other web analytics and making recommendations for improving the delivery of information to customers; AND Experience executing the development and/or publication of web content to maintain content quality and consistent customer messaging. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the United States Patent and Trademark Office, Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Trademark Examination Policy. The position develops and executes trademark web communication strategies to identify customer segments, improve digital engagement, and support delivery of clear, accessible information through effective online communication.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Trademark Examination Policy, Customer Service and Support
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Come work for the Patent and Trademark Office we have been ranked as one of the best places to work in the federal government! The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has been serving the economic interests of America for more than 200 years. We are responsible for granting US intellectual property rights for patents and trademarks. The USPTO is headquartered in Alexandria, Virginia, and has over 12,000 employees. For more information about the USPTO, please visit the USPTO Jobs Website.
MajorDuties: The physical worksite for this position is located in Alexandria, Virginia. Presence at the Alexandria, VA campus is required for this role, as it includes on site functions that must be performed in person. Position may be eligible for situational telework in accordance with agency policy/business unit discretion. The agency currently allows for 52 hours of telework per leave year. You'll make an impact in this role if: You excel at developing and providing oversight and direction for short and long-term planning in setting the business unit's overall customer communication strategy focused on web presence. You bring expertise in identifying methods and practices to mine customer feedback/information from a variety of resources including website traffic statistics, usability-testing data provided by third-party vendors, call center inquiries, online surveys, focus groups and other sources. You thrive in coordinating all trademark-related content published or posted for customers on USPTO public-facing websites and Trademarks intranet under the purview of the Trademarks business unit. You enjoy establishing and maintaining effective working relationships at multiple levels within the Trademarks business unit and across the USPTO, to develop messages that accurately address informational needs of trademark customers.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the United States Patent and Trademark Office, Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Trademark Examination Policy. The position develops and executes trademark web communication strategies to identify customer segments, improve digital engagement, and support delivery of clear, accessible information through effective online communication.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Trademark Examination Policy, Customer Service and Support
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Come work for the Patent and Trademark Office we have been ranked as one of the best places to work in the federal government! The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has been serving the economic interests of America for more than 200 years. We are responsible for granting US intellectual property rights for patents and trademarks. The USPTO is headquartered in Alexandria, Virginia, and has over 12,000 employees. For more information about the USPTO, please visit the USPTO Jobs Website.
MajorDuties: The physical worksite for this position is located in Alexandria, Virginia. Presence at the Alexandria, VA campus is required for this role, as it includes on site functions that must be performed in person. Position may be eligible for situational telework in accordance with agency policy/business unit discretion. The agency currently allows for 52 hours of telework per leave year. You'll make an impact in this role if: You excel at developing and providing oversight and direction for short and long-term planning in setting the business unit's overall customer communication strategy focused on web presence. You bring expertise in identifying methods and practices to mine customer feedback/information from a variety of resources including website traffic statistics, usability-testing data provided by third-party vendors, call center inquiries, online surveys, focus groups and other sources. You thrive in coordinating all trademark-related content published or posted for customers on USPTO public-facing websites and Trademarks intranet under the purview of the Trademarks business unit. You enjoy establishing and maintaining effective working relationships at multiple levels within the Trademarks business unit and across the USPTO, to develop messages that accurately address informational needs of trademark customers.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes must be two pages (or less). Resumes should clearly demonstrate the applicant's relevant experience, skills, knowledge and abilities as they pertain to this position. A qualified candidate must possess the following: One (1) year of specialized work experience directly related to the duties of a Publishing and Media Designer? Such duties could include: production of print and digital media business products; edit, produce and write video, audio and print copy that crosses all platforms (print, web, digital platforms, newsletters, social media); prioritize and manage multiple projects in a deadline driven environment; manage daily and weekly production, newsletters, and social media updates; etc. Working knowledge of Adobe and Microsoft products. Can manage multiple concurrent projects effectively. Can work under pressure. Strong project management and time management skills. Strong organization skills. The ability to work in a team environment. Will have excellent presentation skills. Will have excellent communication (written and verbal) skills. In addition to the above qualifications, candidates who possess the following qualifications will be considered "Highly Preferred" or "Best Qualified": Possess a four year degree with a major emphasis in communication arts, visual communication, interactive journalism or emergent media. Will have the ability to evaluate website metrics to identify trends and content strategies. Possess experience in the Adobe Creative Suite and Google Analytics. Applicant meeting the Best Qualifying Criteria/Highly Preferred will be referred to the hiring manager. All other qualified applicants will be referred if requested by the hiring manager. Claimed experience must be verifiable through your resume. Assumptions will not be made.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located at Stars and Stripes Europe, Kaiserslautern, Germany. Incentives and Bonuses Incentives will not be paid.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Kaiserslautern has developed into the largest US military community outside the United States. The city of Kaiserslautern is nestled in the small hills west of the Rhine River Valley, on the edge of the famous German Pfalz forest. Although the climate is changeable much of the time, the area does enjoy many pleasant days with reasonable temperatures. The winter is short and mild with some snowfall. The summer is generally warm and comfortable, with few hot days. Kaiserslautern has over 100,000 residents and an additional 50,000 personnel associated with the American Armed Forces.
MajorDuties: Serves as the Publishing and Media Design (PMD) Content Producer / Designer for Stars and Stripes. Specializes in the production of print and digital media business products.
Responsible for effectively communicating the evolution and benefits of Stars and Stripes business products to the military and civilian communities.

Manages and delivers business and media collateral to Stars and Stripes audiences and the military community. Provides hands-on knowledge in print and digital media, content development and production.
Works closely with Revenue, Editorial, Member Services, Production and Interactive Media to provide execution and delivery of print and digital media projects.

Edits, produces and writes video, audio and print copy that crosses all platforms (print, web, digital platforms, newsletters, social media) in brand voice, based on creative briefs, supplied material and project objectives.
